liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Touch of Grey** (3 reviews): Touch of Grey flowing into Scarlet Begonias, without any fire, makes a fine opener; Reviewer finds this Touch of Grey grounded and skippable, with Jerry sounding bland [21][26][29]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet is livelier than Touch, though Jerry only starts making interesting sounds just before four minutes; The crowd's excited reaction to Scarlet, played in an unusual spot, is fun to hear [26][32]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (2 reviews): Second-set run of Greatest Story, Good Golly Miss Molly and Blue Dress, back to Good Golly, is a highlight; Bertha into Greatest Story, Blue Dress, Good Golly and back to Blue Dress is called pretty hot [21][25]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Scarlet leads into Little Red Rooster; the crowd groaned at the overused song, but the band nailed it [24]
- **My Brother Esau** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this was the only My Brother Esau they ever saw [32]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feelin' Bad** (1 review): Goin' Down the Road ended before Black Muddy River because the crowd kept clapping after Not Fade Away [31]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ajaja**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Akiwowo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Kiyakiya**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **speaking**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Yembela**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Ilere**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Devil with the Blue Dress Medley**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **We Bid You Goodnight theme**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-16.nak300.gidley.115934.flac2448** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 183 min [1]
- **gd1987-09-16.171964.ultramatrix.miller.flac1648**: soundboard; 23 songs; 157 min [5]
- **gd1987-09-16.154308.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 158 min [6]
- **gd1987-09-16.172260.mtx.tobin.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 156 min [8]
- **gd87-09-16.sbd.hinko.22797.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 157 min; rated 4.4/5 by 19 [11]. Said about its sound: Described as a nice soundboard recording [25]
- **gd87-09-16.schoeps.willy.15206.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 154 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [17]. Said about its sound: This audience recording is judged about as good as the rather muddy soundboard [32]

## Around the show

- Bobby has almost a night off here, and Jerry flubs several lyrics from exuberance rather than forgetfulness [22]
- The show had oddities: Good Golly Miss Molly, Devil with the Blue Dress, and a La Bamba tease [31]
- The New York City Percussion Ensemble opened the show [1]
- The New York City Percussion Ensemble opened the show [5]
- The New York City Percussion Ensemble opened the show [6]
- The New York City Percussion Ensemble opened the show [8]
- Jerry seemed to have a new lease on life in 1987-88 after sickness in earlier years; Brent also flourished [22]
- Reviewer hoped for a Dylan cover but none came, the only such miss on this tour [23]
- Reviewer says every Fall '87 show is overshadowed by the 9/18 performance [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-16.nak300.gidley.115934.flac2448**: taped by Ted Gidley; transferred by AndrewF; source: 24bit/48kHz file set: OTS AUD: 2x Nakamichi CM300 w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90's, w/no Dolby. Taped by Ted Gidley. [1]. Also: Nakamichi 300 recording from Gidley; patches cover tape flips, including the end of Scarlet through the start of Rooster [1]
- **gd1987-09-16.171964.ultramatrix.miller.flac1648**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 9, 2025; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [5]. Also: Ultramatrix mix by Miller, pitch-corrected by Scott Clugston, with a patch source tape sent by Tim Dalton [5]
- **gd1987-09-16.154308.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Tim Dalton's AKG 415 source supplies the first 19 seconds of Let It Grow and a patch in Drums into Space [6]
- **gd1987-09-16.172260.mtx.tobin.flac2496**: transferred by Kevin Tobin [8]. Also: Matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in July 2025 [8]
- **gd87-09-16.sbd.hinko.22797.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [11]
- **gd87-09-16.schoeps.willy.15206.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD (Schoeps CMC 34's)>MC*>DAT>CDEAC/SHN by Willy [17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-09-16 Madison Square Garden, New York, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-09-16-madison-square-garden-new-york-ny-usa/) [36]
